title: Amazon steps up social media efforts
summary: Amazon.com Inc is increasing its focus on social media by hiring a director of social media, John Yurcisin, and building a Social Games Group to compete with Zynga. The company, a pioneer in e-commerce, has lagged in social networking but is now integrating social features into its Kindle e-book offerings. This move comes as Amazon aims to leverage social aspects, such as customer reviews, that have already contributed to its success.

title: Novo Nordisk Launches New, Educational E-Book Series for Managing Diabetes
summary: Novo Nordisk has launched a free, 5-volume educational e-book series aimed at helping patients manage their diabetes more effectively in collaboration with their healthcare teams. This series is part of the Cornerstones4Care™ patient support program and is designed to provide accessible diabetes management information, responding to the increasing demand for e-books. The e-books are compatible with major e-readers and available as free Adobe PDFs, covering topics from diabetes overview to carb counting.

title: Oklahoma City's new Whole Foods is green from the ground up
summary: The new Whole Foods Market in Oklahoma City, scheduled to open on Oct. 12, is incorporating numerous green features, including the state's first public electric vehicle charging stations. The store will also use reclaimed materials, high-efficiency appliances, and LED lighting to minimize its environmental impact. This initiative aligns with Whole Foods' "Green Mission Task Force" and their commitment to environmental stewardship.

title: Amazon's Kindle Fire makes splashy debut
summary: Amazon unveiled its Kindle Fire tablet at a competitive price of $199.99, featuring a 7-inch display and Wi-Fi connectivity, aiming to challenge Apple's iPad. Analysts see Amazon as a strong contender due to its content ecosystem and willingness to price hardware aggressively. The Fire runs on Android, backs up wirelessly to Amazon's servers, and leverages Amazon's vast content offerings and retail platform.

title: Amazon unveils $199 Kindle Fire tablet
summary: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos introduced the Kindle Fire, a $199 tablet, aiming to challenge Apple's iPad by expanding the Kindle brand into full-color, multipurpose devices. The Kindle Fire will go on sale Nov. 15 and runs an Android-based software, offering access to various applications and wirelessly backing up content to Amazon's servers. Additionally, Amazon launched new lower-priced Kindle e-readers, including a $79 model and a $99 touch-screen version, putting further pressure on competitors.

title: Amazon releases iPad rival
summary: Amazon has launched the Kindle Fire, a $199 tablet computer, to challenge Apple's iPad, expanding its Kindle brand into full-color, multipurpose devices. CEO Jeff Bezos also introduced new, more affordable Kindle e-readers, intensifying competition with companies like Barnes & Noble in the e-book market. The Kindle Fire, set to release on Nov. 15, is positioned as a platform for various applications, directly competing with the dominant iPad.
